subject: CloudScale private marketplace commission overlay + terms — exec signoff request
messages:
From: Andrew Blake <andrew@cloudscale.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legal@cloudscale.com>
Date: Tue, 7 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: AWS private listing + nonstandard rev-share and payment terms

Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for the demo last week. CloudScale is ready to move forward with a private AWS Marketplace listing, but we need two non-standard items on the offer to close procurement quickly:

- Rev-share: 40% to CloudScale for the first 12 months (they subsidize a big part of onboarding and marketing)
- Payment: Net90 preferred (our procurement is centralized; Net30 creates cashflow friction)

We can commit to a 12-month minimum listed ARR of $480k and will provide a joint marketing fund (details in the attached SOW). We also need co-term billing with our annual contract and a short SLA addendum for onboarding.

Attaching SOC2 and SOW for your legal review. Please advise next steps and whether Redwood can execute Net90 + 40% rev-share on AWS private offers or if we should expect a counter.

Cheers,
Andrew Blake
VP Partnerships, CloudScale
attachments: cloudscale_soc2_report.pdf, cloudscale_sow_v1.docx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Blake <andrew@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 May 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: AWS private listing + nonstandard rev-share and payment terms

Andrew —

Appreciate the details and the SOW. Quick read-through looks promising — congrats on reaching procurement alignment. I need to loop in Deal Desk (Karthik) and Sales Ops (Priyom) to evaluate the economics and risks of the requested 40% rev-share and Net90.

Immediate asks from my side:
- Karthik: can you do a quick P&L impact for first 12 months with 40% rev-share vs. our standard 25%?
- Priyom: confirm whether we can accept Net90 for a deal with a guaranteed ARR commit (CloudScale is offering $480k floor).
- LegalOps: please flag any compliance or marketplace listing blockers in the SOC2/SOW.

I will aim to get back to you with an internal counter or an exec ask within the day.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: (none)
Date: Tue, 7 May 2029 11:23:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: AWS private listing + nonstandard rev-share and payment terms

Lauren / Priyom —

I reviewed the numbers and CloudScale's ask. Headline analysis below (assumes $480k listed ARR, 12 month term):

- With 40% rev-share: Redwood gross revenue = $288k; marketplace fees (AWS) ~12% = $34.6k; estimated hosting & infra allocation = $40k; OPEX + CS = ~$60k. Net contribution before taxes ≈ $153k.
- With our standard 25% rev-share: Redwood gross revenue = $360k; after marketplace fees and similar allocations net contribution ≈ $225k.

Risk / notes:
- Net90 materially increases DSO and exposes Redwood to cashflow and collections risk for smaller customers; mitigations: require an up-front 30% activation invoice or commit to an ARR escrow, or tier Net90 only if CloudScale pays marketing fund on receipt (use milestone triggers).
- 40% rev-share is a sizeable carveout; acceptable only if we get exclusivity on this vertical or a marketing co-fund guarantee worth at least $40k in the first 12 months.
- AWS private offers: we will need Approval by Revenue Ops + Exec signoff for any commission >30% or payment >Net45. Also Legal must confirm co-term billing is enforceable under AWS mechanics.

Proposed counter (Deal Desk):
- Rev-share: 30% for months 0–12, revert to 25% thereafter
- Payment: Net45 standard; allow Net90 for the full period only if CloudScale prepays 30% on signing and the remainder on Net45, OR if they set up an ARR-backed invoice schedule in HubSpot with a purchase order + escrow clause.
- Marketing fund: $40k co-fund committed and payable 50% on listing go-live, 50% in 90 days.

If you agree, I'll prepare a term sheet and we can escalate to Priyom -> Evelyn for final signoff to permit a >30% rev-share and any Net90 concession.

Karthik
Senior Deal Desk Manager

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 May 2029 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: CloudScale private listing request — request for exec clearance

Evelyn —

Forwarding for your visibility and quick signoff. TL;DR: CloudScale wants 40% rev-share (12 months) + Net90. Deal Desk proposes 30% for 12 months + Net45 (or Net90 with 30% prepay / milestone). This is a high-impact strategic partner (channel potential) and they will co-fund $40k marketing.

Why I think we should consider the concession:
- Gains us a strong AWS go-to-market partner in our target vertical (infrastructure ops) — likely to drive pipeline for other customers.
- The $480k ARR floor plus $40k co-fund materially offsets the revenue dilution in year 1.

Conditions I'd attach to any >30% or >Net45 concession:
1) Executive approval (CRO or Head of Revenue) documented in an approval memo.
2) Legal to sign a co-term clause and ensure we can enforce billing cadence through AWS Marketplace APIs.
3) Finance to create an invoice schedule (prepay or escrow) to limit DSO exposure.

Happy to discuss live — timeboxed decision requested by EOD so we can hit CloudScale's procurement window.

—Priyom
Director, Sales Operations

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 May 2029 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: CloudScale private listing request — request for exec clearance

Team —

I reviewed Karthik's impact analysis and Priyom's rationale. I approve the following conditional concessions to enable the listing and close CloudScale's procurement window: 

- APPROVED: 30% rev-share for months 0–12 (not the requested 40%).
- APPROVED: Net60 payment terms (compromise between our Net45 standard and their Net90 ask) with the following required controls:
  * 30% prepayment on signing (captured outside of AWS listing as a Redwood invoice)
  * Remaining balance invoiced Net60 and tied to an ARR schedule in HubSpot; Finance to configure collections triggers.
  * Marketing co-fund of $40k must be documented and payable 50/50 (50% at listing go-live).

Legal to prepare a short approval memo and updated term sheet reflecting co-term billing language we can enforce via AWS Marketplace. This approval is conditional on Legal confirming co-term is feasible with AWS mechanics and Finance signing off on the prepay flow. If Legal flags an issue, we revert to standard catalog listing options.

Priyom / Karthik: please work with Legal and Finance immediately and provide an updated term sheet + DocuSign link. I expect the final package in the next 3 business hours to meet CloudScale's timeline.

Evelyn
SVP, Revenue Operations
attachments: exec_approval_memo_evelyn_20290507.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Blake <andrew@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, LegalOps <legal@cloudscale.com>, aws-marketplace-specialist@amazon.com
Date: Tue, 7 May 2029 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: AWS private listing + nonstandard rev-share and payment terms (Approved with conditions)

Andrew —

Thanks for your patience. Good news — we have conditional executive approval to move forward with a private AWS offer under the following terms: 

- Rev-share: 30% for months 0–12, revert to 25% thereafter
- Payment: Net60 (Redwood compromise). 30% prepayment due on signing; remainder invoiced Net60.
- Marketing co-fund: $40k (50% at listing go-live, 50% in 90 days)
- Co-term billing: Legal to confirm feasibility with AWS; if accepted, co-term will be included in the Docusign term sheet.

Next steps:
1) Karthik will send an updated term sheet (rdw_term_sheet_v3.pdf) and a DocuSign link for the prepay schedule.
2) Legal & Finance will confirm co-term mechanics and collections setup (HubSpot invoice schedule).
3) Once signed and the 30% prepay is received, we will submit the AWS private offer and coordinate listing go-live with the Marketplace specialist.

Please confirm acceptance by EOD so we can generate the DocuSign and lock the timeline.

Best,
Lauren
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
